headline: US bitcoin funds have already lost more money in November than in any month since they launched, while bitcoin trades back near $60,000 on the US Thanksgiving holiday ahead of Friday's roughly $7 billion options expiry.

market.asOf: Read from CoinDesk's markets report at about 11:17 UTC on Thu 26 Nov (18:17 Bangkok); a fresher price page could not be opened this run. CoinDesk gave bitcoin at about $60,500 to $60,800. Use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: Extreme fear: 10 on CoinMarketCap's Fear and Greed Index, per CoinDesk on Thu 26 Nov.

stories.title: US bitcoin funds set a record for money pulled out in a single month
stories.summary: Money has left US spot bitcoin funds for seven trading days in a row, and November's withdrawals are already the biggest since the funds launched in January 2024. US markets are closed for Thanksgiving, so there are no new flows today.
points: US spot bitcoin funds lost a net $453.1 million on Wed 25 Nov, the seventh straight day of outflows, per The Block.
BlackRock's IBIT accounted for $329.7 million of Wednesday's outflow, per The Block.
November outflows total about $5.39 billion so far, about 20% more than the previous record of $4.51 billion in June 2026, per CoinDesk.
The funds are now about $5.02 billion in the red for 2026, after inflows of $35.24 billion in 2024 and $21.37 billion in 2025, per CoinDesk.
US spot ether funds lost $68.5 million on Wednesday, their ninth straight outflow day, per The Block.

stories.title: Bitcoin climbs back above $60,000 as the US marks Thanksgiving, with $7 billion of options expiring Friday
stories.summary: Bitcoin recovered from Wednesday's low near $57,500 as traders betting on a fall were forced to close out. The biggest options bets for Friday's expiry are protection against further drops.
points: Bitcoin was about $60,500 to $60,800 on Thursday morning after a Wednesday low of $57,500, per CoinDesk (read about 11:17 UTC).
About $618 million of leveraged positions were forcibly closed across crypto in 24 hours; 57.2% of the $245 million closed in bitcoin were bets on a fall, per CoinDesk.
About $7 billion of bitcoin options and $0.6 billion of ether options expire on Deribit on Friday 27 Nov, with a put/call ratio of 0.89 for that expiry, per CoinDesk.
Galaxy withdrew its call that the bear market ended in June; its Alex Thorn says a daily close below $58,525 would point to a materially lower low, per The Block.

CoinDesk: $7 billion of bitcoin options expire Friday

stories.title: US steps up action against crypto scams: 800+ defendants targeted, and a $1.37 billion judgment in New York
stories.summary: The Justice Department says it has launched its largest-ever action against crypto fraud, including scam centers in Southeast Asia. Separately, a New York court ordered the founders of the NovaTech crypto Ponzi scheme to pay about $1.37 billion.
points: The Justice Department targeted more than 800 defendants and froze more than $1 billion in stolen crypto with State Department help, per The Block.
A New York state court ordered NovaTech's founders to pay $1,367,023,585, including $232.5 million in interest, per Decrypt.
About 11,000 New Yorkers were among NovaTech's victims, per Decrypt.
The founders have left the US, so collecting the money may be difficult, per Decrypt.

Decrypt: New York wins $1.37B judgment against NovaTech founders

briefs.title: Standard Chartered's crypto custodian Zodia reports a data breach
briefs.summary: Hackers accessed some client and employee company details, contact names and email addresses, found on 24 Nov; Zodia reports no unauthorized transactions and has told regulators, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Spain lets its anti-laundering unit freeze crypto accounts without a judge
briefs.summary: Sepblac could freeze an account for up to 5 business days without a court order under a decree due to take effect on 25 Jan 2027, pending parliament's approval, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: A bill to hold US government bitcoin for 20 years reaches the full House
briefs.summary: H.R. 8957 would bar selling the government's bitcoin for 20 years; it still needs the Senate before this Congress ends on 3 Jan, and Polymarket odds of a reserve before 2027 are below 5%, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Zcash team urges a faster shutdown of its older privacy pool
briefs.summary: About 400,000 ZEC, about 2% of supply, still sits in the legacy Sapling pool; the team set no deadline, per The Block.

briefs.title: Crypto market maker Auros reportedly winding down
briefs.summary: The trading firm is shutting down, according to two people familiar with the matter cited by CoinDesk; the firm did not comment.

briefs.title: Over 1,000 bitcoin mining sites hijacked by faked internet routes
briefs.summary: An attacker redirected mining power for much of November, peaking at 1.9 EH/s; CoinDesk estimates the stolen revenue at under $17,000.

briefs.title: AI-stock selloff hits debt-funded AI infrastructure firms
briefs.summary: The Nasdaq 100 is down as much as 17% from its peak, and companies such as IREN, Cipher and CoreWeave have fallen as much as 70%, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Franklin Templeton's crypto fund adds Hyperliquid's HYPE
briefs.summary: The EZPZ fund adds HYPE on 1 Dec, per The Block.

calendar.note: Settles at 08:00 UTC, per CoinInsider. About $7 billion of bitcoin options and $0.6 billion of ether options expire, put/call ratio 0.89, per CoinDesk; Bitcoinist gives $6.92 billion. The "max pain" level is $71,000 per Bitcoinist (PiSpace data, 26 Nov) and was $72,000 in a KuCoin post on 24 Nov.

At the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center, per Khaosod English.

calendar.event: Trump Media (DJT) noteholders can demand repayment
calendar.note: Holders of about $1 billion of convertible notes can ask for their money back; the company holds a crypto treasury, mostly bitcoin and CRO, per Finimize (16 Nov).

calendar.event: MSCI removes Strategy (MSTR) from its indexes
calendar.note: Takes effect after the close on 30 Nov. MSCI-linked funds hold about 13 million MSTR shares, about 3.1% of the total, by Strategy's own estimate reported by Cointelegraph.

calendar.event: ISM manufacturing PMI (Nov), job openings (JOLTS, Oct); Fed's Bowman testifies to the House
calendar.note: ISM: October was 55.5, per Newsquawk. JOLTS: September was 7.52 million, per the BLS. Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman appears at the House Financial Services "Oversight of Prudential Regulators" hearing, per the Fed's calendar. CrowdStrike's earnings call is at 5:00pm ET and Marvell's at 4:30pm ET.
October was +86,000, per InvestingLive. Salesforce holds its earnings webcast at 5:00pm ET.

Forecasts differ: U.S. Bank cites a +101,000 consensus and forecasts +98,000 with 4.1% unemployment itself; Continuum Economics expects +95,000 and 4.1%. October payrolls rose 165,000 with unemployment at 4.1%, per Continuum Economics.
Markets expect a rate hike, not a cut: CME FedWatch put the chance of a quarter-point hike at 97.8% on 25 Nov, per KuCoin News. Press conference at 2:30pm ET, per the Fed's calendar.
